title: An Improved Upper Bound for the Turán Number of the Hexagon
summary: For a graph $F$, the Turán number $\operatorname{ex}(n,F)$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of $F$. Determining the Turán numbers of even cycles is a central problem in extremal graph theory and remains open in general. For $C_6$, the best previous upper bound was due to Füredi, Naor, and Verstraëte [Advances in Mathematics, 2006], who proved that, for sufficiently large positive integer $n$, $$ \operatorname{ex}(n,C_6) \leq λn^{4/3}+O(n)<0.6272 n^{4/3}, $$ where $λ$ is the real root of $ 16λ^3-4λ^2+λ-3=0$.
